Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Fix issue 14449: ToolStrip DPI change issue in .NET 10
Issues.Body:
Backport of #14454 to release/10.0

Fixes #14449 

This issue was introduced by PR [#13582](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/13582), when we drag the ToolStrip control on screens with different DPI settings, the call stack history is [WmDpiChangedBeforeParent](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/blob/5d71425a3fecf8f72a57679b53bd2b5035ca0059/src/System.Windows.Forms/System/Windows/Forms/Control.cs#L11562) -> [RescaleConstantsForDpi](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/blob/5d71425a3fecf8f72a57679b53bd2b5035ca0059/src/System.Windows.Forms/System/Windows/Forms/Controls/ToolStrips/ToolStrip.cs#L3725). However, within the WmDpiChangedBeforeParent method, [OriginalDeviceDpiInternal](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/blob/5d71425a3fecf8f72a57679b53bd2b5035ca0059/src/System.Windows.Forms/System/Windows/Forms/Control.cs#L470-L475) and DeviceDpiInternal retrieve the same value, which will cause the RescaleConstantsForDpi method in the ToolStrip class to fail to execute as expected.

## Proposed changes

-  OriginalDeviceDpiInternal = DeviceDpiInternal; is effectively a no-op in the common case: the setter uses DeviceDpiInternal as the default value to remove the stored property, so after DeviceDpiInternal is updated later in this method, OriginalDeviceDpiInternal will again resolve to the new DPI. This means other code that relies on OriginalDeviceDpiInternal != DeviceDpiInternal during/after the DPI-change path will still observe them as equal. So consider capturing oldDeviceDpi first, updating DeviceDpiInternal to the new DPI, and then assigning OriginalDeviceDpiInternal = oldDeviceDpi so it is persisted (mirroring how Form sets OriginalDeviceDpiInternal = e.DeviceDpiOld).

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- ToolStrip DPI change correctly in .NET 10.

## Regression? 

- Yes- regression PR https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/13582.

## Testing

- Manually
- Unit test

## Risk

- Minimal

Issues.Title: Fix RadioButton focus rectangle visibility when an image is assigned
Issues.Body: Fixes #15289 ## Root cause The shared button layout calculates the focus rectangle from the union of the text and image bounds. Issues.Title: Fix ComboBox crash during handle creation with autocomplete on non-system-DPI monitors
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15286

## Root cause
Starting with .NET 7, per-monitor V2 DPI handling can scale an explicitly assigned font during `Control.OnHandleCreated`, synchronously invoking `ComboBox.OnFontChanged`.

When `AutoCompleteMode` is not `None`, `ComboBox.OnFontChanged` unconditionally recreates the handle. This destroys the handle while its initial creation is still in progress. The nested creation attempt returns early because `States.CreatingHandle` is set, leaving the remaining ComboBox initialization without a valid handle.

.NET 6 has the same autocomplete-related handle recreation logic, but its handle-creation DPI path does not perform the font scaling that triggers this reentrancy.

## Proposed changes

- Skip autocomplete-related handle recreation in `ComboBox.OnFontChanged` while `States.CreatingHandle` is set. Autocomplete initialization proceeds afterward as part of the existing handle-creation flow.
- Preserve handle recreation for font changes after handle creation has completed.
- Add regression tests covering DPI-related font changes during handle creation and normal font changes afterward, across all autocomplete modes.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Prevents applications from crashing when adding a ComboBox with an explicitly assigned font and a non-None autocomplete mode on a monitor whose DPI differs from the system DPI.

- Yes

- Minimal

Issues.Title: Fix ComboBox Binding Sequence Affecting Binding Ability of Other Controls
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #9272


## Proposed changes

- Update `Control.UpdateBindings()` to activate bindings with the actual `BindingContext` only when the control is created.
- Use a `null` binding context for controls that are not yet created, deferring binding activation until control creation.
- Add a regression test covering a `ComboBox.SelectedValue` binding added before sibling bindings on controls placed within an initially hidden tab.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Adding a `ComboBox.SelectedValue` binding first can cause bindings on sibling controls within an initially hidden tab to be activated before those controls are created.
- Properties such as `Label.Visible` can be incorrectly set to `false` during early binding activation, making the control remain hidden and giving the appearance that its binding is broken.

## Regression? 

- Yes

## Risk

- Low. The change aligns `Control.UpdateBindings()` with the existing created-gated behavior in `Binding.SetBindableComponent`. Bindings for controls that are not created will remain deferred until the controls are created.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->


## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before

When `ComboBox.SelectedValue` is bound before bindings on controls within an initially hidden tab, a bound `Label` can be incorrectly set to `Visible = false` before control creation and remain hidden after selecting the tab.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e83d5c88-4221-47f3-b1a9-616535bb9733

### After

Bindings on controls within an initially hidden tab are deferred until the controls are created. After selecting the tab, the `Label.Visible` binding is active, and the label displays the correct initial visibility state.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36935409-a8f6-4252-a082-ec719281bc51

## Test methodology <!-- How did you ensure quality? -->

- Added the `ComboBox_SelectedValueBindingAddedFirstOnHiddenTab_DoesNotBreakSiblingBindings` regression test in `ComboBoxTests.cs`.
- Created a `Form` and `TabControl` with two tab pages, with a `Label` and `CheckBox` placed on the second, initially hidden tab page.
- Added the `ComboBox.SelectedValue` binding first, followed by the `CheckBox.Checked` and `Label.Visible` bindings to the same data model.
- Verified that selecting the second tab and creating its controls activates the `Label.Visible` binding.
- Verified that the label is initially visible and is not incorrectly forced to `Visible = false`.
- Verified that changing `CheckBox.Checked` updates the model and changes `Label.Visible` to `false` as expected.

## Accessibility testing  <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

- This change does not introduce new UI or modify the visual structure of existing controls.

## Test environment(s) <!-- Remove any that don't apply -->

- Windows Forms unit test environment.
- `Form` containing a `TabControl` with two tab pages.
- `ComboBox`, `CheckBox`, and `Label` bound to an `INotifyPropertyChanged` data model.
- Second tab page initially hidden and its child controls not created when the bindings are added.

Tested binding activation before and after creating controls on an initially hidden tab page.

Issues.Title: Fix ToolStripTextBox and ToolStripComBoBox in the toolbar do not scale well when bringing items down from 100% to 300%
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #8277, #5116


## Proposed changes

- Update hosted `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` controls to correctly synchronize their fonts when the parent `ToolStrip` DPI changes.
- Scale the hosted control width once using the old and new DPI values, and calculate the height from the preferred size after applying the correct font.
- Update the hosted control's `DeviceDpi` to prevent its font from being scaled more than once.
- Preserve custom fonts by scaling them once, while controls using the default font receive the new `ToolStrip` default font.
- Refresh the layout after applying the updated font and size.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` display an incorrect font and control size when an application moves between monitors with different DPI settings under Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness.
- After this change, the hosted text box and combo box correctly update their font, width, and height for the destination monitor.

## Regression? 

- Yes

## Risk

- Low. The change modifies DPI scaling behavior for hosted `ToolStrip` controls. The main risk is incorrect font or size scaling during repeated DPI transitions, especially for controls using custom fonts.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->


## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before

When moving the application from a 100% DPI monitor to a 150% DPI monitor, `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` retain an incorrect font and use their previous width and height.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06ae5ac0-2bae-46ed-8e48-36dc8b9c8e78

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/995fd887-999d-49c0-add4-d6ffacc2db38

### After

When moving the application between monitors with different DPI settings, `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` correctly update their font, width, and height to match the destination monitor.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c5e76e5-a08c-4cbe-aa1c-ac426c4cade0

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c60ebf9-961c-493c-8ace-0e4fe4937198

## Test methodology <!-- How did you ensure quality? -->

- Added the `ToolStrip_RescaleConstantsForDpi_ScalesHostedTextBoxAndComboBox` regression test under a Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness scope.
- Verified that `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` widths scale correctly when changing from 96 DPI to 288 DPI.
- Verified that the hosted `TextBox` and `ComboBox` font heights increase after scaling to 288 DPI.
- Verified that the original widths and font heights are restored when scaling back from 288 DPI to 96 DPI.
- Verified that hosted controls using the default font receive the new `ToolStrip` default font and that custom fonts are scaled only once.

## Accessibility testing  <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

- Verified that the DPI scaling changes do not introduce new accessibility failures or regressions.
- Verified that the hosted controls remain visible, correctly sized, and usable after moving the application between monitors with different DPI settings.


## Test environment(s) <!-- Remove any that don't apply -->

- Windows Forms unit test environment using Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness.
- DPI scaling tested from 96 DPI to 168 DPI and from 168 DPI back to 96 DPI.
- `ToolStrip` containing `ToolStripTextBox` and `ToolStripComboBox` hosted controls.


Tested hosted control font and size updates during repeated DPI transitions under Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness.

Issues.Title: New .NET 11 WinForms design-time analyzer help links redirect to an incorrect webpage
Issues.Body:
### .NET version

.NET 11 SDK: 11.0.100-rtm.26477.103

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Not tested/verified

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

New .NET 11 WinForms design-time analyzer

### Issue description

The help links for the new .NET 11 WinForms design-time analyzer diagnostics redirect to an incorrect webpage.

This issue can be reproduced with both errors and warnings. 
For example:
- WFO3000: The diagnostic code itself provides a clickable help link.
- WFO3002: A help link is displayed in the diagnostic description.

Clicking these links redirects to Bing instead of the corresponding WinForms analyzer documentation.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c94bedb0-01eb-48bc-a3b0-f423c09a85c6

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a WinForms project targeting .NET 11.
2. Trigger a new WinForms design-time analyzer diagnostic, such as WFO3000 or WFO3002.
3. Open **Error List** in Visual Studio.
4. Click the help link associated with the diagnostic:

- For **WFO3000**, click the diagnostic code.
- For **WFO3002**, click the help link shown in the description.

5. Observe the webpage opened in the browser.
